Books of related interest

TAITTIRĪYA ĀRAṆYAKA

With the Comm. of Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara Miśra and an Eng. Introduction by T.N. Dharmadhikari

(3 volumes bound in one)

Edited by A. Mahadeva Sastri and K. Rangacarya

THIS TREATISE belongs to the Taittirīya School of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda and is ‘āraṇyaka’ because it is to be recited by a Vrati in the midst of araṇya (forest). This is a reprint of the earlier edition brought out in the Government Oriental Library Series Nos. 26, 27 and 29, Mysore. In this edition, the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka has been divided into 8 Prapāṭhakas. Prapāṭhaka 1 deals with Aruṇaketucayana. Prapāṭhaka 2, i.e. Svādhyāya Brāhmaṇa deals with the rite of Sacred Thread, Twilight Worship, Kuṣmāṇḍa Sacrifice, Initiation and vows. These two Prapāṭhakas belong to the Kaṭha School of Black Yajurveda. Prapāṭhaka 3 compiles formulas for Caturhotraciti, Puruṣakṛticiti, Upahoma. Caturhotraciti is the same as Brahmaciti or Brahmamedha. Prapāṭhaka 4 deals with the Pitṛmedha and cremation rites. Prapāṭhaka 5 comprises the Taittirīya Upaniṣad, divided into 3 vallis: Śikṣā, Brahma and Bhṛgu. Prapāṭhaka 6 constitutes, Nārāyaṇopaniṣad known as Yājñiki. Prapāṭhakas 7, 8 contain the Pravargya formulas and their Brāhmaṇa.

item.title: 1 Introduction
item.description:
[[P3]]

1 The Pravargya Ritual

The oldest portions of the wonderfully complex structure of Vedic texts are interlaced with numerous references to ritual acts and ceremonies.

The exact contents of the ritual acts and ceremonies referred to are often no longer recoverable. Among these references mention is made of a probably simple hot-milk offering, gharmá,¹ to the Aśvins, the twin-gods connected with dawn and sunrise. item.title: 2 Text and Translation
item.description:
[[P45]]

01: The Pravargya as the head of the Sacrifice

This anuvāka contains the mythological story of the origin and purpose, the purākalpa, of the Pravargya ceremony in the form of the story of Makha. See Introduction section 3.4 and Hillebrandt, Vedische Mythologie:414-54; Keith, Religion:112; Rönnow, “Zur Erklärung des Pravargya etc.":113ff, esp. 127; Eggeling, SBE 44, p. xlvi-l; van Buitenen, Pravargya:16ff; Gonda, Aspects: 167ff; Kashikar, “Mahāvīra"; and Heesterman, “The Case of the Severed Head” in: Essays in Indian Ritual, Kingship and Society, Chicago 1985. In the introduction of the TĀ edition C (p. 27-28), a translation of this anuvāka is quoted from Muir, Sanskrit Texts IV, p. 112.

item.title: Appendix
item.description:
1: The Place of Sacrifice

The Place of Sacrifice for a Pravargya that forms part of a Soma Sacrifice The regular performances of the Pravargya (TĀ 5, anuvāka 4-8) take all place in the Pracinavamsa, except that the Adhvaryu and his assistant leave the hut through one of the doors, in order to milk the cow and goat (see anuvāka 7, and note 81). The twice daily heating of the Pravargya vessel takes place on the western or pravṛijaniya mound. At the end of each performance, except at the time of the final disposal, the implements are put on the Samraḍ-asandi or Emperor’s Throne. The Patni-sālā (Wife’s Hall) is at the west of the Prācina-vamsa.
